speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) for the past eight years, what are the annual median and average lengths of service of foreign nurses in restructured hospitals; and (b) if the data is not available, whether there has been an increasing or decreasing trend in the lengths of service of foreign nurses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just ask what is the current shortfall in terms of foreign nurses that we are planning to hire?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could I ask whether there is a timeline for this and when do we expect to be able to meet this shortfall?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Deputy Speaker, I thank the Member for the questions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I wanted to go back to the points that had been raised in the discussion during the Healthier SG White Paper debate and the further Parliamentary Questions (PQs) that had been raised in the past.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: A large portion of these numbers would be for nurses.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is something that we have already been working on and the target is by 2030 to up these numbers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The clusters are doing their best to step up recruitment efforts.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Minister Ong had earlier indicated that even in as far as our local intake is concerned, we have looked at the intakes at the schools, the Institute of Technical Education (ITE), Polytechnics and Universities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These are the different efforts that are being put in place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have discussed this extensively at the White Paper debate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: With all the efforts in place, we are hoping to see a better number.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are not just looking at the shortfall.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is also important for us to also see what other needs there may be.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, these are the aspects we look at for the efforts we are doing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I have those numbers, but those numbers include both local and foreign.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am asking if we have a number specifically for foreign nurses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I think we debated this before that the problem is that a lot of the foreign nurses have left.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And that is why there is a huge burden on the local nurses now.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I am just wondering what is the shortfall in terms of foreign nurses and how we intend to meet that shortfall.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I mentioned earlier, we do not only just look at shortfall and work towards just filling up the shortfall.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are also having to look at the demands of the public and what are the needs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do not necessarily find it valuable to make that distinction.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As much as possible, we try and see what are the different avenues and channels for us to increase this intake and we are making efforts on that front.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have explained how we have worked with the clusters to see how we can see to the well-being of the nurses and improve the stature of their career, career paths as well as increasing the intake from the different schools.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is an aspect that we are doing and that will never be enough – to reach the 82,000 that we are looking for.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Hence, we have to complement that with the efforts we are doing in recruitment of overseas nurses.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is the multi-pronged approach that we are taking and this is something that will, hopefully, increase and improve the situation in time to come.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know we are trying to increase the intake but it will take some time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If today, we increase the intake, it will be a couple of years down the road before we see the effects in the wards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, the fastest way to alleviate the problem is perhaps to see whether we can increase the hiring of foreign nurses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In a few weeks, a few months, we could hire a huge number that will help to alleviate the current problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: That is why I keep pushing for information on what is MOH's expected number of foreign nurses that we are hoping to hire and how we are hoping to reach that.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Minister Ong Ye Kung shared yesterday some of the countries we are looking at.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: With those plans out there in the public, some of the local nurses might feel a bit more assured that help is on the horizon and not three or four years away.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have had a lot of extensive debates.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Member has filed a lot of questions on this matter.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are looking at the specific avenues and different avenues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I also hope that the Member could assist to explain to some of the nurses whom he is in touch with, who are concerned about this situation, that we are doing whatever is necessary to retain the nurses who are within our healthcare system right now; we are doing what we can to increase the numbers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That is the more important focus, rather than talk about just the shortfall.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because we are talking about different avenues and different things have to change over time.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We need to adjust because what is important to us is that we meet the demands, we address the current concerns that the healthcare sector is facing right now.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we will do whatever it takes in the different aspects – increasing the intake from the local workforce, as well as to increase our recruitment.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: That is something the Member is quite familiar with.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai, do you have a supplementary question?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How many of them will be foreigners and how many of them will be locals?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Deputy Speaker, I think I am repeating myself ad nauseum.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think Mr Leong Mun Wai was also present at the discussion of the Healthier SG White Paper, at the debate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And Mr Louis Ng has also filed several PQs on this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: You may want to check our responses in response to those PQs.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This number is in different categories and what is important for us is that we address the demands, the needs of the sector as well as the needs of the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I hope that Members can also support us by assuring the healthcare workers that this is a matter that is very close to the heart of the Ministry.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We have been engaging extensively with the clusters, we have been engaging extensively with the healthcare workers and trying to give them some respite.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Everyone has a role to play in this – MOH, the public – in helping to alleviate the concerns and the challenges that our healthcare workers are currently facing.
